name: Jessner lymphocytic infiltration of the skin

criteria.description: Presence of asymptomatic or mildly pruritic erythematous papules, plaques, or nodules primarily on the face, neck, or upper back
Dense perivascular and periadnexal lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis without epidermal involvement or mucin deposition
Exclusion of lupus erythematosus, cutaneous lymphoma, and other granulomatous or inflammatory dermatoses
Negative antinuclear antibody (ANA) and other autoimmune serologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Typical clinical presentation with compatible histopathology and exclusion of other similar dermatoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by skin biopsy; no standardized diagnostic criteria exist.

laboratory: Normal complete blood count and inflammatory markers
imaging: Not typically required; imaging generally normal
other: Skin biopsy showing perivascular and periadnexal lymphocytic infiltrate without epidermal involvement or mucin deposition

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of epidermal changes such as interface dermatitis
Positive ANA or other autoimmune serologies
Atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism on biopsy
Progressive clinical course with systemic involvement

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging or ulcerating skin lesions
Systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats
Histopathologic evidence of atypical lymphocytes or epidermal involvement
references: Jessner M. Lymphocytic infiltration of the skin. Arch Dermatol Syphilol. 1953;67(5):483-490.
Wollina U. Jessner-Kanof lymphocytic infiltration of the skin: clinical and histopathological features. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2005;19(3):309-313.
